results.title: SK hynix Developing New NAND Products for KV Cache Demands - Seoul Economic Daily
results.content:
KV cache is temporary data required for graphics processing units (GPUs) to handle AI computations. As AI data surges, the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity for storing KV cache is reaching its limits. In response, SK hynix plans to develop new products that mount high-capacity NAND products near the GPU, allowing them to serve as an additional KV cache repository. [...] SK hynix (000660.KS) said on the 29th during its second-quarter earnings conference call that it is developing new NAND product families such as "near-GPU storage" driven by key-value (KV) cache offloading. results.content:
Accelerator-in-memory: its AiM/AiMX processing-in-memory line, which needs a volume commitment to move from prototype to product.

High Bandwidth Flash (HBF): the new NAND-based tier it is standardizing with Sandisk to hold the exploding KV cache in AI inference.

Custom HBM (cHBM): base dies co-designed to a customer’s AI chip and workload, where the margin and lock-in of the next cycle will live. results.title: LAM: What is the KV Cache Hiding? - by Claus Aasholm
results.content:
The Chinese memory makers were not part of the same oversupply cycle that crushed Samsung and SK Hynix. They were still in build-out and ramp mode throughout 2022-2023, constructing greenfield capacity from scratch. So their equipment spending continued even as Korean and US memory makers slammed the brakes. [...] I am writing this from sunny Zurich, where I have just delivered a live presentation of the state of the Semiconductor supply network and the drivers of demand and supply. For a lowlander like me, it is very challenging to operate at the dizzying altitude of 400 meters. The highest point of the island of Lolland, where I live, is 30 meters, so I am literally in the dead zone. Any errors in this article will be solely due to the lack of oxygen. ### An analysis of LAM's Q1-2026 result and long term growth prospects

Claus Aasholm

∙ Paid

This period of the year is always quite challenging from a business intelligence perspective, as Q1 reporting rolls in quickly. As most Semiconductor companies have their fiscal year aligned with the calendar year, Q4 reporting is later and more spread out than in other quarters. This overlaps with the quick reporting of the Q1 numbers.

results.title: SK hynix strives to secure capital through ADR listing - The Korea Times
results.content:
The ADR plan is one of SK hynix’s recent efforts to secure capital. The company has been reportedly requesting the government to ease regulations on holding firms and rules separating commerce and finance, so that it can establish special purpose companies involving financial investors and raise funds for expanding its fabs. [...] The details of the rule remain uncertain, but trusting treasury shares to a depository institution for an ADR offering could be deemed a disposal of those shares, because the company will not have control on the shares. Through this, SK hynix can find a way out from the mandatory cancellation.
